title: pumllint requirement-traceability report
description: The output of `pumllint trace <paths> -f json`: the coverage matrix between a requirements inventory and the diagrams that reference them, both directions plus unknown references. This shape is a public contract; changes are deliberate and release-noted (drift-guarded by tests/test_schema.py). Requirement `id` values are stable identifiers: future matrix columns (process step, component, contract) will arrive as additive optional properties on the requirement row, never by reshaping v1. The verification column arrived on 2026-09-09 exactly that way: `verified`/`verifiedBy` on the row, `unknownFeatureReferences`, `unlinkedFeatures` and five summary counts, all present only when `--features` was given — without it the payload is the v1 shape. Later the same day feature-side sites gained `scenario`/`scenarioLine` and the summary `scenarioCount`, then `unlinkedScenarios` and `unlinkedScenarioCount`, the same way.

requirements.description: One row per inventory ID, in inventory order.

unknownReferences.description: IDs referenced by diagrams but absent from the inventory — a typo, or a stale inventory.

unlinkedDiagrams.description: Diagrams whose reference carriers (name, title, header, footer, caption, notes) contain no requirement ID.

unknownFeatureReferences.description: Verification side, present only when --features was given: IDs referenced by feature files but absent from the inventory — the same typo detector as unknownReferences, applied to the tests. Kept apart so unknownReferences keeps meaning 'a diagram said it'.

unlinkedFeatures.description: Verification side, present only when --features was given: feature files (name and text) that reference no requirement ID.

unlinkedScenarios.description: Verification side, present only when --features was given: scenarios no reference is attributed to, in files that reference at least one ID. Derived from the attribution rules: a Feature or Rule tag reaches every scenario under it, a file-level reference (file name, header, Background) reaches none. A file with no reference at all is an unlinkedFeatures row and its scenarios are not repeated here.

featureCount.description: Verification side (only with --features): feature files scanned.

scenarioCount.description: Verification side: scenarios declared across the scanned feature files (Scenario, Scenario Outline, Example headings; an outline counts once whatever its Examples expand to; 0 for a non-English dialect).

verifiedCount.description: Verification side: inventory IDs realized by a diagram AND referenced by a feature file. The denominator is coveredCount, never requirementCount — an unmodelled requirement is already uncoveredCount, and one gap must not count twice.

unverifiedCount.description: Verification side: inventory IDs realized by a diagram but referenced by no feature file — modelled but untested, the --fail-on-unverified set. verifiedCount + unverifiedCount = coveredCount.

id.description: The requirement ID exactly as it appears in the inventory — the stable join key for any wider traceability matrix.

verified.description: Verification column, present (together with verifiedBy) only when --features was given: at least one feature file references this ID. A row fact — true on an uncovered row means tested but not modelled.

verifiedBy.description: Verification column: the feature-file sites referencing this ID — one per file and scenario the reference is attributed to, at the line of its first occurrence (0 when the ID is carried by the file name).

site.description: A reference site: the file (a diagram, or on the verification side a feature file), its declared name (the diagram name, or the Feature: heading; null when absent) and the line of the first text containing the ID — 0 when a feature-side ID is carried by the file name.

featureSite.description: A feature-file reference site: the file, its Feature: heading (null when absent), the line of the first text carrying the ID (0 when carried by the file name), and the scenario the reference is attributed to by Gherkin's tag rules — a Feature tag belongs to every scenario in the file, a Rule tag to every scenario under it, a tag line above a scenario to that scenario, text inside a scenario to that scenario; null (with scenarioLine 0) when the reference is the file's own: its name, the feature header or description, a Rule description or the Background.

scenario.description: The scenario's title as written after Scenario:/Scenario Outline:/Example: ('(unnamed)' when empty), or null for a file-level site.

scenarioLine.description: The line of that scenario's heading, where the reader opens; 0 for a file-level site.

name.description: The Feature: heading, null when the file has none.

scenarioLine.description: The line of the scenario's heading.

name.description: The Feature: heading, null when the file has none.

diagramType.description: An open set (new parsers add values) — consumers must tolerate unknown strings.
